title: Fix Chip Label Font Size Consistency
description: Chip labels (window titlebar/footer/navbar chips, chapter/section/subsection heading chips) render with wildly different text heights across contexts even though they should all use the same fixed chip font size. Root cause: print/script.ts emits \semio@chrome@font@chip and \semio@chrome@font@body as `em`-relative LaTeX lengths (e.g. "0.6em"). In LaTeX, `em` inside \fontsize{...}{...} resolves against whichever font is ambient at the exact call site *before* \selectfont switches font — and chip font is invoked from many different ambient contexts (KOMA setkomafont for chapter/section/subsection which may run under different active sizes, navbar/footer text, table captions, paragraph muted caps). So the same nominal "0.6em" token yields different absolute point sizes depending on where it's used, while only the box width should vary dynamically. Fix: emit chip/body font tokens as absolute `pt` sizes (following the existing px*0.75 pt-conversion convention already used for stroke tokens in the same generator function) instead of `em`, so text height is identical everywhere and only chip width adapts to content. Update print/script.ts's emitSemioTokensSty, regenerate print/tex/semio-tokens.sty via the nx/bun script command, and rebuild+visually verify a couple of the print documents (e.g. report, zwischenbericht) to confirm chip label heights now match across window chrome, navbar, footer, and heading levels.
summary:
Fixed chip label font-size inconsistency across window chrome, navbar/footer, and heading chips (chapter/section/subsection). Root cause: `emitSemioTokensSty` in print/script.ts emitted `\semio@chrome@font@chip` / `\semio@chrome@font@body` as `em`-relative LaTeX lengths. Inside `\fontsize{...}{...}\selectfont`, `em` resolves against whichever font is ambient at the call site *before* `\selectfont` applies — and the chip font macro is invoked from many differing ambient contexts (KOMA `setkomafont` for chapter/section/subsection, navbar/footer text, paragraph muted caps, table captions), so the same "0.6em" token rendered at different absolute point sizes depending on where it was used.

Fix: emit `\semio@chrome@font@chip` and `\semio@chrome@font@body` as absolute `pt` sizes (px * 0.75, matching the existing stroke-token conversion convention already used in the same generator) instead of `em`, so chip text height is now identical everywhere and only the chip box width adapts dynamically to its label content. Updated the `\providecommand` fallback defaults in semio-window.sty to match. Regenerated print/tex/semio-tokens.sty via `bunx nx run @semio-tech/print:generate`. Verified by compiling the `report` template with `bun ./print/script.ts` and visually inspecting the rendered PDF (navbar chip and heading chips now share identical text cap-height, widths differ per label).
